transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-12
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Maya Tran (Redwood SE), Priya Venkatesh (Redwood CSM); Amina Khan (CTO, Summit Edge), Carlos Rivera (Head Infra), Lena Park (Security Engineer), Samir Patel (Procurement), Evan Cho (App Dev)

Auto-summary: high-level security intake to qualify deployment mode. Discussed SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS and data retention.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side, I'm Jordan, AE for the account, Maya is our solutions engineer, Priya on success.
[00:14] Amina: Hi thanks, I'm Amina, CTO at Summit Edge — appreciate the time. We want to evaluate Redwood for inference across a payments fraud product. Security is the gating factor.
[00:28] Jordan: Totally get it. before we dive, can you share quickly where you are on compliance? SOC2, ISO, anything required by partners?
[00:35] Carlos: We're SOC2 Type II in progress, expecting audit close in Q4. We do ISO 27001 internal for a few teams but not company wide yet. main ask is proof of encryption at rest and key control.
[00:49] Lena: And we have contractual retention requirements for logs - some partners require seven years for certain PII access logs.
[00:58] Maya: Ok that helps. I'll outline how Redwood handles each area — and also call out Hosted, Dedicated, Private differences.
[01:10] Jordan: Quick note — this call is discovery, we'll follow with a tech deep dive once we know the constraints.
[01:18] Amina: Sounds good. Lina — sorry Lena, lead on security questions?
[01:23] Lena: Yes. first question: do you support BYOK to an HSM? we need keys that we control.
[01:30] Maya: Yes. Redwood Private and Dedicated can integrate with customer KMS/HSM. hosted API support is usually industry standard AES at rest with provider-managed keys, but for BYOK and HSM we recommend Private or Dedicated with KMS integration. There was a small note — sometimes we see the term "BY [OK]" in transcription, heh.
[01:52] Carlos: For Dedicated, do you run in our VPC or in a Redwood-managed VPC with peering? network isolation details?
[02:00] Maya: Two main patterns: Dedicated in a customer VPC (VPC-hosted using our appliance) or Dedicated in Redwood-managed VPC with strict peering and private links. For Private/on-prem we can run in your data center behind your LAN. We'll share a deployment checklist.
[02:20] Evan: Latency matters — our models will be called from client apps, target 100-150ms p95 token latency. is that realistic?
[02:29] Maya: For short prompts on GPU-backed models that's feasible with Dedicated and good placement; hosted can be lower but depends on region, model size, and batching. There's always tradeoff with cost.
[02:44] Samir: Procurement question — do you have SOC2 and ISO artifacts we can review? and do you have a data processing agreement?
[02:53] Jordan: Yes, we will send SOC2 summary, our ISO certifications where applicable, and standard DPA. I'll attach them after the call.
[03:06] Lena: Audit logs — what granularity do you provide? we need immutable logs for request/response metadata, admin actions, and key lifecycle events.
[03:17] Maya: We provide request-level logs, admin activity logs, and a separate audit stream. For Private, logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. For Hosted we can provide an export and retention controls; currently hosted default retention is 90 days but we have enterprise add-ons for longer retention.
[03:36] Lena: 90 days won't cut it — many of our contracts say three to seven years. how would you approach that?
[03:42] Maya: For long-term retention we usually integrate with customer S3 or a log archive through secure transfer. For Dedicated/Private we can push logs directly to customer-managed storage with configurable retention policies. There's an extra cost for long-term archival.
[03:56] Carlos: Any concerns around PII in model inputs/outputs? we need controls to redact or isolate certain fields.
[04:05] Jordan: Redwood has prompt-level controls and we can recommend a schema enforcement approach — also prefix/KV caching choices so sensitive prefixes aren't cached. Maya — mention KV cache nuance?
[04:15] Maya: Right. we do automatic KV caching for seq models; you can disable prefix caching or use token filtering. For sensitive fields we advise client-side redaction or a middleware to strip PII before sending. For Private deployment you can also disable caching entirely.
[04:34] Amina: Regarding SSO — we use Okta and need SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning.
[04:40] Jordan: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. Priya can run through the exact connector types post-call.
[04:50] Priya: We'll send the Okta app manifest and SCIM endpoint docs.
[04:56] Lena: RBAC — can we define custom roles and admin scopes? we don't want devs touching keys.
[05:03] Maya: Yes, RBAC is configurable. you can create roles limited to invocation only, restricted to model selection, or admin roles that can manage keys. For Hosted, admin actions go through our control plane; for Private you manage control plane and can enforce stricter RBAC.
[05:20] Evan: How detailed are the change logs? if someone rotates a key, do we get a timestamped record with actor?
[05:27] Maya: Yes — key lifecycle events are logged with actor identity. For Hosted that actor is a user identity mapped via SSO; for Private we can map to your LDAP/IdP.
[05:36] [06:00] Jordan: let's talk about encryption in transit and at rest — standard TLS for transit, AES-256 for rest, and HSM/Cloud KMS options for key management. any specific vendor requirements?
[06:12] Carlos: We prefer AWS KMS or customer HSMs for certain contracts. can you bring your own KMS key to Hosted?
[06:20] Maya: BYOK on Hosted is limited — we typically recommend Dedicated or Private for full BYOK with HSMs. For Hosted we have provider-managed KMS with customer tenant separation.
[06:35] Lena: What about data residency — can we ensure data never leaves eu-west-1?
[06:41] Jordan: Yes, region pinning is supported for Dedicated and Private; Hosted supports region endpoints where available but we'd need to confirm model availability per region.
[06:54] Samir: Contractual — do you support audit rights and pen tests?
[07:01] Priya: We support vendor security assessments, pen test summaries upon NDA, and standard audit rights in enterprise contracts.
[07:10] Lena: For logs we need WORM (write once read many) capability for certain archives — is that achievable?
[07:17] Maya: Yes, if you archive to your S3 with object-lock or WORM support, that covers the retention requirement. Redwood will forward logs but the storage policy is customer-managed in that case.
[07:30] Amina: From an ops perspective, how do upgrades/rollouts happen? we need controlled canaries and rollback windows.
[07:38] Maya: Redwood has rollout controls: canaries, staged rollouts, and automatic fallback. For Dedicated we can schedule maintenance windows. Private gives you control over upgrade timing.
[07:50] Carlos: On the networking side, will IP allowlists be static? we need to open firewall rules only once.
[07:56] Jordan: For Dedicated we can provide static egress IPs or ranges. For Hosted IPs are subject to change unless you use private link or peering.
[08:08] Evan: Any built-in data classification or PII detection?
[08:13] Maya: We have a classification hook and can integrate with your DLP to tag or block certain inputs. It's more mature on Private/Dedicated where you can insert custom middleware.
[08:25] [08:40] Lena: What about model explainability — need to capture prompts and model config at time of response for auditability.
[08:48] Maya: We can log model config, seed, prompt hash, and response metadata. For full transcript storage we recommend customer-managed storage due to retention.
[09:00] Amina: How do you handle multi-tenant isolation? if we use Hosted, will another tenant ever see our data?
[09:09] Jordan: Hosted isolates tenants logically; no cross-tenant data access. dedicated/Private provide stronger isolation, with Private being single-tenant.
[09:18] Carlos: Do you support on-prem air-gapped deployment?
[09:22] Maya: Yes, we have an on-prem package for air-gapped environments — it requires a bit more setup and support contract.
[09:30] Samir: For procurement, we'll need SLAs. what uptime and latency SLAs are offered for Dedicated?
[09:38] Jordan: Dedicated has an SLA that covers uptime and best-effort latency targets; we can share the SLA PDF. Private is negotiable by contract. For Hosted, we provide best-effort availability and published uptime metrics.
[09:54] [10:10] Amina: Ok, next, any red flags around exporting logs for legal eDiscovery?
[10:18] Maya: Export is supported — we can automate snapshots to your archive. For very large exports we coordinate with infra to ensure throughput.
[10:27] Lena: Are there limits on who can request exports? need to ensure only compliance/legal can request them.
[10:33] Maya: Requests are gated by RBAC — only roles with export permission can trigger an export.
[10:40] Carlos: We also need to ensure admins don't accidentally exfiltrate keys. can you have dual-control for key rotation?
[10:47] Jordan: We can support approval workflows for key operations in Private, and for Dedicated we can set up workflows integrated with your ticketing system.
[10:56] Evan: Will Redwood run model retraining or fine-tuning on our data?
[11:01] Jordan: By default Redwood does not train or store data for model training. We can contractually specify no training.
[11:08] [11:30] Samir: Pricing question tied to retention — long-term log retention is priced separately?
[11:36] Maya: Yes archival storage and long-term retention are billed separately. we'll provide an estimate.
[11:43] Lena: Any certifications around hardware security modules?
[11:47] Maya: We integrate with major cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and can support customer HSMs that meet FIPS 140-2/3 depending on deployment.
[12:00] Jordan: Let's capture next steps — Jordan to send SOC2/ISO docs, Maya to draft Dedicated sizing, Carlos to send network diagrams, Lena to send retention list.
[12:12] Amina: Good. When should we reconvene for the sizing call? next week Tue or Wed works.
[12:18] Jordan: We'll propose Wednesday 2026-08-19 15:00 UTC.
[12:23] Maya: I'll include a pre-call checklist so Carlos can have VPC details ready.
[12:30] Lena: Also please include the specific log schema we can expect for audit ingestion.
[12:35] Priya: We'll add that to the doc bundle.
[12:40] Amina: Thanks everyone, helpful conversation.
[12:44] Jordan: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the package and calendar invite.

End of transcript.
